qs.q:
Couch-surfing — Which person…

A=Aida (budget traveller, prefers peace and quiet, but hosted a Korean girl and her father cycling to Barcelona)
B=Benjamin (travelling USA with girlfriend, stayed with Seattle couple who shared couch-surfing stories from Europe)
C=Chris (hosted four Hungarians who cooked goulash and kuglóf, now wants to visit Budapest)
D=Dana (wanted to couch-surf with friend Bella to Scotland, parents said no, Bella had tough time alone)
E=Erin (solo Caribbean trip, Dutch host had no manners, was looking for babysitter, Erin hitch-hiked away)
F=Fabian (solo Beijing, stayed in luxurious apartment, host in Paris half the week, had keys and restaurant coupons)

0. likes taking a rest during travels without being disturbed by unknown people? [A=Aida]
1. stayed with a host of European origin?
2. has already made up their mind about their next destination?
3. was amazed by the host's accommodation?
4. had a really difficult time during the last experience?
5. has never had any couch-surfing experience of their own?
6. introduced their traditional cuisine to their guests?
7. was entertained by their hosts' couch-surfing experience?
8. was talked into a couch-surfing experience?
9. is couch-surfing at the moment of speaking?
10. was pleasantly surprised by their guests' gratitude?
11. needs approval for couch-surfing?
12. couch-surfs on their own?
items: 1 — stayed with a host of European origin?
2 — has already made up their mind about their next destination?
3 — was amazed by the host's accommodation?
4 — had a really difficult time during the last experience?
5 — has never had any couch-surfing experience of their own?
6 — introduced their traditional cuisine to their guests?
7 — was entertained by their hosts' couch-surfing experience?
8 — was talked into a couch-surfing experience?
9 — is couch-surfing at the moment of speaking?
10 — was pleasantly surprised by their guests' gratitude?

qs.q:
Climbing Everest

"The southern side is very AVALANCHE-PRONE. This is why we chose to climb NORTH."

Why did Karen and Mark climb on the north side of Khan Tengri?
A Because there are fewer people climbing the north side.
B Because the last day of the climb is less difficult.
C Because there are fewer avalanches.
D Because it was more challenging.
opts: Because there are fewer people climbing the north side.
Because the last day of the climb is less difficult.

qs.q:
Climbing Everest

"We never fought UNLESS we were EXTREMELY TIRED."

While climbing mountains, Karen and Mark…
A fought when they had to make difficult choices.
B would end up fighting after a long debate.
C fought when they were exhausted.
D never had a serious argument.
opts: fought when they had to make difficult choices.
would end up fighting after a long debate.

qs.q:
Climbing Everest

"Having PRIOR EXPERIENCE AT HIGH ALTITUDES was key, though."

According to Mark, what was most important in preparing for the climb?
A They had climbed high mountains in the past.
B They raised their self-confidence doing yoga.
C They had regular sessions at the gym.
D They had altitude training sessions.
opts: They had climbed high mountains in the past.
They raised their self-confidence doing yoga.
They had regular sessions at the gym.

qs.q:
Climbing Everest

"There we experienced another delay due to A LEAKING OXYGEN TANK."

Why did Karen and Mark have to postpone the final stage?
A Because of strong winds that lowered visibility.
B They hadn't yet adjusted to the high altitudes.
C The temperatures were uncommonly low.
D Because of problems with climbing gear.
opts: Because of strong winds that lowered visibility.
They hadn't yet adjusted to the high altitudes.
Because of problems with climbing gear.

qs.q:
Climbing Everest

"We used the INTERNET to get updates about their plans."

In base camp, the couple and members of the other expeditions they knew…
A walked over to each other's tents to hear the news.
B communicated through neighbouring teams.
C exchanged information through the internet.
D spent their time hanging out together.
opts: walked over to each other's tents to hear the news.
spent their time hanging out together.

qs.q:
Climbing Everest

"Karen usually led and set the pace, but after weeks of climbing, we agreed WE'D SWAP ROLES at regular intervals."

On summit day…
A Mark and Karen took turns leading.
B Mark took on the role of motivator.
C Karen set the climbing goals.
D Karen led the climb.
opts: Mark and Karen took turns leading.
Mark took on the role of motivator.

qs.q:
Planning a garden

"Garden design is like getting dressed. You don't get dressed by putting on every piece of clothing you like. (19) _____. Too many gardens are made up of every plant that looks nice in the garden centre."

A Give the garden a rhythm that draws the eye from one place to another.
B If all else fails, plant lots of Verbena bonariensis: it fits in everywhere.
C And you shouldn't approach your garden this way either.
D It is true that they are sometimes hard to maintain.
E However, it's rare that this happens flawlessly.
F They are dynamic, changing spaces.
G Bend them all at once if necessary.
H Then choose plants to match.
opts: A — Give the garden a rhythm that draws the eye.
B — If all else fails, plant Verbena bonariensis.
C — And you shouldn't approach your garden this way either.
D — They are sometimes hard to maintain.
E — However, it's rare that this happens flawlessly.
F — They are dynamic, changing spaces.
G — Bend them all at once if necessary.
H — Then choose plants to match.
